'''Alison Butler''' is a [[Professors in the United States#Distinguished (teaching / research) professor|Distinguished Professor]] in the Department of [[Chemistry]] and [[Biochemistry]] at the [[University of California, Santa Barbara]]. She works on [[bioinorganic chemistry]] and metallobiochemistry. She is a Fellow of the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]] (1997), the [[American Chemical Society]] (2012), the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]] (2019), and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] (2019).<ref name="Members - Alison Butler">{{Cite web|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/butler/alison/members/butler|title=Members - Alison Butler|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-08}}</ref> She was elected a member of the [[National Academy of Sciences]] in 2022.<ref>{{cite web | url=http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220503174757/http://www.nasonline.org/news-and-multimedia/news/2022-nas-election.html | url-status=dead | archive-date=May 3, 2022 | title=2022 NAS Election }}</ref>

== Education ==
Butler studied at [[Reed College]], graduating in 1977.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|url=https://blogs.reed.edu/chemistry_news/2018/05/alison-butler-77-receives-acs-bader-award-in-bioinorganic-chemistry/|title=Alison Butler '77 Receives ACS Bader Award in Bioinorganic Chemistry {{!}} Chemistry News|last=alan|date=May 14, 2018|website=blogs.reed.edu|language=en-US|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref> She started in immunology, but moved into chemistry to work with transition metals.<ref name=":2">{{Cite news|url=http://research.universityofcalifornia.edu/profiles/2011/10/alison-butler.html|title=Research Profiles - Alison Butler|work=University of California Research|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref> She worked with Professor Tom Dunne on ''An intramolecular electron transfer study: the reduction of pyrazinepentaaminecobalt (III) by chromium (II)''.<ref name=":1" /> She earned her PhD at [[University of California, San Diego]] in 1982 under Robert G. Linck and Teddy G. Traylor.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web|url=http://www.chem.ucsb.edu/people/alison-butler|title=Alison Butler|website=www.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-08}}</ref>

== Career ==
Butler worked as a postdoctoral fellow at [[University of California, Los Angeles]] with [[Joan S. Valentine]] and at [[California Institute of Technology]] with [[Harry B. Gray]].<ref name=":3" /> She was appointed to the faculty at [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] in 1986.<ref name=":3" /> Here she was awarded an [[American Cancer Society]] Junior Faculty Research Award.<ref name=":3" /> She was awarded the 34th [[University of California, Santa Barbara]] Harold J Plous Award.<ref name="Members - Alison Butler"/>

She looks to discover new siderophores, small molecules that bind iron in microorganisms.<ref name=":4">{{Cite news|last=Julie Cohen|url=http://www.news.ucsb.edu/2017/018264/ironing-out-puzzle|title=Ironing Out a Puzzle|date=September 18, 2017|work=The UCSB Current|access-date=2018-10-08|language=en}}</ref> She uses genomics and [[bioinformatics]] to predict new siderophore structures. She explores how siderophores adhere to mica and look at how they can promote surface colonisation.<ref name=":4" /> She identified that siderophores become sticky when wet, which may help to develop underwater adhesives.<ref name="The Current">{{cite news |last1=Tasoff |first1=Harrison |title=Organic Prize for Inorganic Researcher |url=https://www.news.ucsb.edu/2018/019194/organic-prize-inorganic-researcher |access-date=April 13, 2021 |work=The Current |publisher=[[University of California, Santa Barbara]] |date=September 25, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2015/08/150806151357.htm|title=Sticky situation: Researchers study, improve a small molecule that possesses an impressive ability to adhere in wet environments|work=ScienceDaily|access-date=2018-10-11|language=en}}</ref> Her current research considers the uptake of microbial iron, vanadium haloperoxidases in microbial quorum sensing and cryptic halogenation, bio-inspired wet adhesion using catechol compounds, and the oxidative disassembly of lignin.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/butler/alison/research/microbial-iron-uptake|title=Microbial Iron Uptake|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/butler/alison/research/vanadium-haloperoxidases-0|title=Vanadium Haloperoxidases|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/butler/alison/research/bio-inspired-wet-adhesion|title=Bio-Inspired Wet Adhesion|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref> Her research into the bioinorganic chemistry of iron is funded by the [[National Institutes of Health]] and [[National Science Foundation]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Alison|first=Butler|title=The Bioinorganic Chemistry of Iron|url=http://grantome.com/grant/NIH/R01-GM038130-11|journal=Grantome|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nsf.gov/awardsearch/showAward?AWD_ID=1710761|title=NSF Award Search: Award#1710761 - Bioinorganic Chemistry of Catechols: Siderophores, Adhesive Proteins and Biomimetic Analogs|website=www.nsf.gov|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref> She studies how transition metal ions are used by marine organisms.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Butler|first=Alison|date=1998-07-10|title=Acquisition and Utilization of Transition Metal Ions by Marine Organisms|journal=Science|language=en|volume=281|issue=5374|pages=207–209|doi=10.1126/science.281.5374.207|issn=0036-8075|pmid=9660742|s2cid=9538550|url=http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9e93/68215b0e7ef96c0320fb6096780c8db2dd77.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190302161832/http://pdfs.semanticscholar.org/9e93/68215b0e7ef96c0320fb6096780c8db2dd77.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=2019-03-02}}</ref>

In 2012, she became the president of the Society for Biological Inorganic Chemistry, and served until 2014.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/butler/alison/news/378|title=Alison Butler begins term as President of SBIC|date=2012-07-01|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref> She was made a Fellow of the [[American Chemical Society]] in July 2012.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/butler/alison/news/262|title=Alison Butler named in the 2012 Class of Fellows of the American Chemical Society|date=July 23, 2012|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref> She delivered the 2016 Douglas Eveleigh Endowed Lecture at the [[Waksman Institute of Microbiology]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://labs.chem.ucsb.edu/butler/alison/news/606|title=Alison gives the Douglas Eveleigh Endowed Lecture at the MBL sponsored by the Waksman Foundation|date=July 19, 2016|website=labs.chem.ucsb.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-10-11}}</ref> In 2018, she was awarded the [[American Chemical Society]] Alfred Bader Award for her work on siderophores.<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite journal|url=https://cen.acs.org/articles/96/i2/Alfred-Bader-Award-Bioinorganic-Bioorganic.html?type=paidArticleContent|title=Alfred Bader Award in Bioinorganic or Bioorganic Chemistry|website=cen.acs.org|doi=10.1021/cen-09602-awards8|access-date=2018-10-11|doi-access=free|url-access=subscription}}</ref> 
In 2019, she was elected to the [[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]], received the American Chemical Society's Arthur C. Cope Scholar award for excellence in [[organic chemistry]], and received the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s Inorganic Mechanisms Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.amacad.org/news/2019-members-announcement|title=New 2019 Academy Members Announced|publisher=[[American Academy of Arts and Sciences]]|date=April 17, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Arthur C. Cope Scholar Awards |url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/bytopic/arthur-cope-scholar-award.html |publisher=[[American Chemical Society]] |access-date=April 13, 2021}}</ref><ref name="The Current"/><ref>{{cite web |title=Inorganic Mechanisms Award |url=https://www.rsc.org/prizes-funding/prizes/archives/inorganic-mechanisms-award/ |publisher=[[Royal Society of Chemistry]] |access-date=April 13, 2021}}</ref> Butler also received the 2019-2020 Faculty Research Lecturer Award, the highest honor that University of California, Santa Barbara faculty can bestow on their members.<ref>{{cite web |title=Awards |url=https://senate.ucsb.edu/~awards/ |publisher=[[University of California, Santa Barbara]] |access-date=April 13, 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Prior Year Recipients |url=https://senate.ucsb.edu/~awards/recipients/detail.cfm?V=F4D86D05CCFB67AB0A74C0668B2D31EAB7C59ED10C03CDF5 |publisher=[[University of California, Santa Barbara]] |access-date=April 13, 2021}}</ref>
